questions.question_content: Which of the following HTML elements can be used to break a text and continue it in the next line in an HTML document?
questions.explanation: The line break element <br> ends the current line so the text continues on the next line.

questions.question_content: Which of the following is used to navigate to other resources or to a specific element in an HTML document?
questions.explanation: The anchor element <a> creates a hyperlink that can take the user to another resource or to an element on the same page.

questions.question_content: Which of the following options is the correct syntax to add an HTML anchor element to our website?
questions.explanation: An anchor element puts the destination URL in the href attribute of the start tag, the link text between the tags, and ends with </a>.

questions.question_content:
Write a program that builds an HTML anchor element from a URL and the link text.

Remove leading/trailing spaces from both lines. If the link text is empty, use the URL as the link text.

#### Input
The first line contains the URL (no spaces inside it).
The second line contains the link text (may be empty).

#### Output
A single line in the form `<a href="URL">TEXT</a>`.

#### Sample Input
```
https://www.google.com
Google
```

#### Sample Output
```
<a href="https://www.google.com">Google</a>
```

test_cases.input:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajmahal
Read more about Taj Mahal

questions.question_short_text: Open External Links in a New Tab
questions.question_content:
A website wants every **external** link (one whose URL starts with `http://` or `https://`) to open in a new tab using `target="_blank"`. Other links (same-page links like `#contact` or pages like `about.html`) open normally.

Each input line has a URL, then a single space, then the link text (the text may contain spaces). If a line has only a URL (no space), the URL itself is the link text.

#### Input
The first line contains an integer `N` (1 <= N <= 50).
Each of the next `N` lines contains a URL followed optionally by a space and the link text.

#### Output
For each line print one anchor tag:
- external: `<a href="URL" target="_blank">TEXT</a>`
- otherwise: `<a href="URL">TEXT</a>`

Finally print `External links: K`, where `K` is the number of external links.

#### Sample Input
```
3
https://www.google.com Google
#bio My Bio
about.html About Us
```

#### Sample Output
```
<a href="https://www.google.com" target="_blank">Google</a>
<a href="#bio">My Bio</a>
<a href="about.html">About Us</a>
External links: 1
```

test_cases.input:
3
https://www.google.com Google
#bio My Bio
about.html About Us
test_cases.output: Google My Bio About Us External links: 1

http://example.com Example Site
https://www.youtube.com Watch Videos Here

https://www.ccbp.in Profile Image External links: 2

questions.question_content:
Given one line of HTML, find the `href` value of every anchor element (`<a ...>`) in the order they appear, and say what kind of link it is.

Rules:
- Only anchor elements count: a start tag `<a` followed by whitespace or `>` (tag name is case-insensitive). Other tags such as `<link href="...">` or `<abbr>` are ignored.
- Inside the anchor's start tag, attributes are separated by whitespace. The attribute name `href` is case-insensitive, may have spaces around `=`, and its value is in double quotes or single quotes. Attributes like `data-href` are not `href`.
- An anchor without an `href` attribute is skipped.
- Kind of link: value starting with `#` -> `same page`; starting with `http://` or `https://` -> `external`; anything else -> `other page`.

#### Input
A single line of HTML. Attribute values never contain `<` or `>`.

#### Output
For each href found, print `VALUE -> KIND`. If no href is found, print `No links found`.

#### Sample Input
```
<p>Visit <a href="https://www.google.com" target="_blank">Google</a> or read my <a href="#bio">Bio</a></p>
```

#### Sample Output
```
https://www.google.com -> external
#bio -> same page
```

test_cases.input: Visit Google or read my Bio
